text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Security forces cordonned the ministerial palace to prevent hundreds of media workers from staging a sit-in to protest a government ban on scores of television and radio stations.
-The new parliament to hold its first general meeting on October 22.
-Maronite Patriarch Sfeir: The constitution calls for equality between the Lebanese. The incompetent government supresses the weak.
-Prime Minister Hariri promised to carefully consider the situation of workers in banned radio and television stations.
-The General Labour Confederation insists on demonstrating on October 10.
-A decree approved by the cabinet will reduce commissions charged on transactions by the Beirut Stock Exchange.
-President Hrawi might resign after the new cabinet is formed and Hizbollah to Damascus to discuss the future of al-Manar television.
